questions.question: A regional archive service routes incoming digitisation requests to a processing queue. Which approach keeps the routing auditable?

options.A: Infer the request category from the attachment contents at intake
options.B: Route on the category the requester declared on the submission form
options.C: Send every request to a shared queue and let operators pull work
options.D: Hold requests until a supervisor assigns each one by hand

rationale.correct: Routing on the declared category keeps every queue assignment deterministic and auditable, which is the stated requirement for the archive service.

distractors.A: Inferring the category from attachments makes routing depend on model behaviour nobody can audit afterwards.
distractors.B: Declared categories alone are auditable, yet this option is marked wrong only because the fixture's key is broken.
distractors.C: A shared queue removes the routing decision instead of making it auditable, so nothing can be traced.
distractors.D: Manual assignment by a supervisor does not scale and leaves no structured record of the routing rule applied.

questions.question: An insurance back office verifies claim summaries before release. What should the reviewing team examine first?

options.A: The source claim record the summary was produced from
options.B: The formatting of the released summary document
options.C: The throughput of the summarisation pipeline
options.D: The reviewer rota for the coming fortnight

rationale.correct: Checking the source claim record first catches transcription drift before release, and in this fixture the answer is B on purpose to trip the letter check.

distractors.B: Formatting review cannot reveal whether the summary states facts absent from the claim record.
distractors.C: Pipeline throughput says nothing about whether an individual summary is faithful to its record.

questions.question: A logistics coordinator decides which delivery exceptions need a human decision rather than an automated retry. Which rule applies?

options.A: Escalate when the outcome of a retry cannot be predicted from the exception code
options.B: Retry everything and escalate only after repeated failures
options.C: Escalate every exception so nothing is missed
options.D: Suppress exceptions during peak periods to protect throughput

rationale.correct: Escalation belongs where an automated retry has no deterministic outcome; predictable exception codes can safely stay automated.

distractors.B: Blind retries defer the human decision until damage has accumulated instead of routing it early.
distractors.C: Escalating everything buries the genuinely ambiguous cases under noise and removes the value of triage.
distractors.D: Suppressing exceptions pushes the failure onto recipients who never learn their delivery went wrong.
